findings.title: Win push-in frames Pip and an empty bench; the delivered robot and the green dock lamp are never shown
findings.problem: The garage's payoff is the robot driving its route and arriving at the dock, where the dock lamp turns green (room.ts:112-113 lightUp). When it arrives, snap().won flips and the camera pushes in on winFocus(). For any station, winFocus() returns station.table + 0.5 m (game.ts:398), and the push-in uses distance 7 and pitch .5 offset 2.2 m to the right (game.ts:373). In the run the robot stopped at (-8.1, 0.35, -5.6), about 9.4 m from the bench. The win frames (garage-models-65-delivered, -66-result, -77-win-moment) show Pip cheering in front of the bench, the scope reading 'Press PULSE' and an empty TEST STAND sign. The robot, the dock and the green lamp are all off-screen. Orbiting after the win (garage-models-78-win-orbit-to-dock) shows only the empty rolling road. The one moment where the fixed machine visibly works, which the player has waited three jobs for, is never framed. The result card also covers the right half of the frame. During the drive itself Pip stays seated or standing at the bench. At zoom 9 the robot is out of frame for most of the 11 s route (garage-models-64-driving); only at the default zoom 26 is it visible (garage-models-76-drive-4s).
findings.fix:
1) Add an optional `winFocus?():T.Vector3` to the Station interface (src/stations/types.ts). In game.ts:398 use `this.station?.winFocus?.() ?? station.table+.5`. In GarageBench return the robot's body translation once `this.delivered`, i.e. DOCK at (-8.1, 1.0, -5.6), aimed between the dock and Pip.
2) In startDrive() (station.ts ~258), after leaveBench(), auto-walk or teleport Pip to a 'watch spot' about (-5.8, -3.6) facing the dock, so the push-in (distance 7) frames Pip and the robot together inside the centre 70%.
3) While `driving`, have the camera follow the robot: set the focus to lerp(Pip, robot, .6) and clamp the zoom to at least 18 until delivered.
4) Delay the result card about 1.2 s after `delivered` so the green dock lamp and confetti read first.
findings.verify: Rerun mockups/review5/tools/garage-models/d-drive.mjs. The win-moment shot must show Pip, the robot at the dock and the lit dock lamp, all inside the centre 70% of the frame (DR-11). Add an assertion to tests/station-garage.spec.ts that projects the robot's position into NDC at won and checks |x|,|y| < .7.
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced the full solve in v1.mjs. When won flips, the robot is at (-8.1, .35, -5.6) while the push-in frames Pip and the bench, because winFocus = station.table+.5 (game.ts:398) and the push-in uses distance 7, pitch .5, offset 2.2 m right (game.ts:373). verify-garage-models-13-win-early and -14-win-late show Pip cheering at the bench, the scope reading 'Press PULSE' and the result card on the right. The robot, the dock and its green lamp (room.ts:112-113) are not in frame, which breaks DR-11. Two small corrections: the station default zoom is homeZoom 18.5 (game.ts:396), not 26. Fix item 4 mostly exists already: the card panel appears at once and the grade lands after 1400 ms (game-ui.ts:221), so the problem is framing, not timing.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/verify-garage-models-12-driving.jpg (default zoom: the robot is visible mid-route while Pip stands idle at the bench)
v1.mjs log: robot at t11 = (-8.1, .35, -5.6), Pip still at (.37, -1.48)
src/ui/game-ui.ts:221 (1400 ms delay before the grade lands)
findings.fix_correction: Keep fix 1: an optional Station.winFocus(); GarageBench returns the midpoint of Pip and the robot once delivered, or the dock lamp plus a .4 lerp toward Pip, with distance raised to about 10 so both fit. Do not teleport Pip; snapping the player breaks the feel. A plain auto-walk is also unnecessary if the focus is the Pip–robot midpoint. For item 3, only bias the camera toward the robot while driving, and let any player orbit or zoom input override it so the camera stays player-controlled. Drop item 4, because the 1.4 s delay already exists. Instead, hold the card's panel (not only the grade) until about 1.2 s after delivered.

findings.fix:

I re-measured the start shot (rows 220–760) and 2.85% of pixels pass r>220, 170<g<215, b<90, the same in the norim shot. verify-garage-models-01/03 show yellow crate stacks at the right wall, yellow mail carts near spawn, a yellow chair, and a yellow-drawered cabinet column behind the scope (also in the bench view, -07). findings.title: The job robot is an identical copy of the two decor robots beside it; only the marker says which one to carry
findings.verify: Hide the HUD via g.page CSS (.objective, .marker). In garage-models-10-robot-pad a first-time viewer should name the job robot from the model alone. Retake that shot and garage-models-01-start.
findings.verify_reason: The code bears this out. The job robot is robotMesh() with default TEAL/TEAL2 (station.ts:105). The decor robot at 4.4 is robotMesh(TEAL) because the test is x>5?'#4aa3d8':TEAL (room.ts:87), so it is identical. The one at 8.4 differs only in its blue body. findings.fix_correction: The eye and lamp materials are reassigned every frame in update() (station.ts:376), so the 'broken' blink must be folded into that line (for example `!this.onStand&&blink?hot('#ff5a4d',2):...`); a separate assignment would be overwritten. The rest of the fix (recolour or dim the decor robots, add a REPAIR tag) is fine.

findings.title: Objective marker rides on the carried robot instead of pointing at the test stand
findings.problem:
Step 1's `at()` is `this.bot?.body.translation()??PAD` (station.ts:97). The marker therefore always hovers over the robot, including while Pip carries it. In garage-models-50-carry-robot and -51 the yellow marker cone sits on top of the robot in Pip's hands. Nothing on screen points at the destination (the test stand behind the bench, at (0.7, -4.45)). The stand is also hidden behind the bench at the default camera (garage-models-12-test-stand, -14), so a new player carrying the robot does not know where to go. The objective card says 'behind the bench', but the world marker contradicts it.

The marker itself is a pale, translucent, un-outlined flat cone. In front-on views it reads as a yellow flashlight beam or a fan wedge (garage-models-21-wheels-right-o180, -31), and it fails DR-44 (outline, 2-tone shading).
findings.fix:
1) station.ts:97: `at:()=>this.game.held===this.bot?STAND:(this.bot?.body.translation()??PAD)`.
2) While the robot is held, also light a footprint decal on the stand's top: a PlaneGeometry(2, 1.3) with a dashed-outline canvas like the bench sockets' `dashed` texture, pulsing in opacity .4–.9. This gives the stand its own 'put it here' cue (the AGENTS 7 snap zone is 2.6 m, station.ts:337).
3) Marker model (game.ts, wherever the marker cone is built): make it opaque with toon shading and an outline. Use two parts, a cone plus a sphere cap, with a dark ink rim. Keep its height ≥24 px at the game camera.
findings.verify: Rerun c-solve.mjs. In garage-models-50/51 the marker must sit over the test stand while the robot is held. Add a spec step to tests/station-garage.spec.ts: after KeyE on the robot, the current step's at() must be within .5 m of STAND.
findings.verify_reason: station.ts:97 at() returns the robot's body translation, and objectives.ts:117-118 puts the marker at that x,z at y≈2.1. verify-garage-models-05-carry and -06-carry-mid show the yellow cone riding on the carried robot, with no world cue at the stand until the prompt changes to 'Set the robot on the stand' within 2.6 m (station.ts:456). In garage-models-23 the cone, seen low or reversed, reads as a flat yellow wedge or fan. One part of the description is wrong: the marker is not translucent. It is an opaque MeshBasicMaterial with its colour multiplied by 1.5 and outlines off (objectives.ts:97-98), so it blooms pale and has no ink edge.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/garage-models-23-lamp-backright-o180.jpg (marker reads as a yellow wedge, top right)
findings.fix_correction: Item 1 is correct. For item 3, the marker is built in src/ui/objectives.ts:97-98, not game.ts. Use a toon-shaded material with an outline in place of the unlit MeshBasic (colour ×1.5) that blooms.

findings.title: Robot faces away from the bench camera: the reboot cue (red eyes) is edge-on exactly when it matters
findings.problem:
placeOnStand() sets the robot's rotation to identity (station.ts:340). robotMesh's face (screen and eyes) is at local +x (room.ts:57-58), so on the stand the face points +x, to the right. The bench camera looks along -z from the +z side, so the player sees the robot's left flank: cargo bin, head side and two wheels (garage-models-54-bench-view, -56-bench-arc, -57).

When the controller reboots, the eyes turn red and the robot wobbles (station.ts reboot() and the eye-material swap in update). That is the in-world failure cue at the faulty part (DR-28, DR-47), and from the bench only a 5 px antenna bead shows it (red dot at about (895,170) in -57). The face's 'personality' is also never seen at the bench.

Parked on the pads, all robots have rotation π/2 (garage.ts:8, room.ts:87), so their faces point at the back wall. At the default game camera the player only ever sees the robots' backsides (garage-models-01-start, -10). The face reads only when orbiting 180° (-11, -23) or while driving (-76).
findings.fix:
1) Place the robot on the stand angled toward the bench: rotation.y = -π/2 + .35, so the face points +z with a slight turn and reads three-quarter from the bench camera. Rotate the rolling-road rollers to match (room.ts:77: the roller axis becomes 'x'; roller positions (±.33, z ±.36)).
2) Make the red-eye reset unmissable: scale the eyes up 1.4× during resetFlash, and burst 'star' particles at head height (already in reboot()). Also flash the CONTROLLER lamp on the board, which the bench camera does see.
3) Park the pad robots nose-out: rotation -π/2 in garage.ts:8 and room.ts:87 (bot.root.rotation.y=-Math.PI/2). Move the chargers' 'plug' to the robots' cargo end, so the faces look into the room at the game camera.
findings.verify: Retake garage-models-56/57 (PULSE with nothing fitted). Both red eyes must be visible and ≥8 px each in the bench view. Retake garage-models-01-start: the robot faces (eyes) are visible from the default yaw.
findings.verify_reason: placeOnStand sets identity rotation (station.ts:340) and the face is at local +x (room.ts:57-58), so from the bench camera you see the left flank: cargo bin plus head side (verify-garage-models-07, -09). The pad robots have rotation π/2, which turns their faces toward the back wall (garage-models-10). I downgraded to P2 because the reset is already shown at the bench by other cues. The CONTROLLER lamp on the board turns red during resetFlash (station.ts:377), and it is visible red in verify-garage-models-09-arc-later at about (843,527). The antenna lamp is also red, and the scope says 'RESET at shutdown!'. The face is a secondary cue.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/verify-garage-models-09-arc-later.jpg (CONTROLLER lamp red, antenna lamp red, face edge-on)
src/stations/garage/station.ts:377 (ctrlLamp already flashes red on reset)
findings.fix_correction: Drop the 'also flash the CONTROLLER lamp' part of item 2; station.ts:377 already does it. Item 1 (rotation.y = -π/2+.35, rollers rotated to axis 'x') is technically correct. Also move the harness end (room.ts:81) with it so it does not land in a wheel.

findings.title: TEST's five cycle lamps are hidden behind the PULSE/TEST buttons at the bench camera
findings.problem: The five cycle lamps are how the bench shows a TEST's progress and its pass or fail per start/stop. They are spheres of radius .024 m at pod-local (-.12+k*.06, .1, -.2) (station.ts:179). That puts them at the back edge of the pod, directly behind the two big buttons: cyl r .17 at z -.06, about .12 m tall (station.ts:176-177). From the bench camera (distance 6.8, pitch .86) the buttons hide them. In the TEST crop only one or two specks show between the buttons (garage-models-74-test-cycle-lamps). In the bench views (-54, -60) the row is invisible. A lamp's on-screen diameter would be about 5 px even if unoccluded, below the DR-59 8 px floor. They are visible only from the back of the room (garage-models-15-bench-front-o180), where no player looks during a test. So the 'five cycles' a player is asked to wait through have no readable in-world counter.
findings.fix: Move the lamp row to the pod's front lip in front of the buttons: pod-local z +.2, y .09, spacing .09, radius .035. Seat each lamp in a dark bezel (cyl(.045,.05,.02) INK) so it is outlined. Alternatively add the five lamps as a strip on the robot's cargo lid (cargo-local y .30), so the robot itself shows the cycles. Keep hot('#8dffb0',1.4) and hot('#ff7a6b',1.4) for pass and fail.
findings.verify: Rerun d-drive.mjs. The crop garage-models-74 at +1.2 s into TEST must show five distinct lamps, each ≥8 px, with 2–3 lit green. Then compare against the cycle count.
findings.verify_reason: Geometry: the lamps sit at pod-local (-.12..+.12, .1, -.2) with r .024, behind buttons at z -.06 with r .17 whose tops reach y≈.18 (station.ts:176-179). I reproduced a TEST at +1.2 s: in verify-garage-models-11-test-lamps-crop only one or two specks show between PULSE and TEST, and none are readable in the bench view. Two claims are overstated. First, the lamps are not only visible from the back: they show at pitch .5 (garage-models-77 and verify-13, '●●●' between the buttons). Second, they do not show per-cycle pass or fail, because cycleFail is decided before the run and every lamp takes the same colour (station.ts:223,370). The TEST verdict is given at once by a toast and the job advance (station.ts:224-229), so this is a readability polish issue, not P1.

findings.title: Kickback arc still whites out the switch, the node and the ACROSS SWITCH socket for over 1 s (still open from research F4)
findings.fix:
station.ts:186-189:
- arcCore → hot('#e8f8ff',1.2), so it stays under the bloom threshold.
- Give each arc segment an INK outline twin: the same cyl at radius .02 in toon(INK), rendered first.
- arcGlow: size .35, opacity .35. Fade it out over 120 ms, not with arcT.
- arcLight: intensity ≤ 1.5, distance 1.
- Re-jitter the bolt for .3 s, then hold a 0.6 s scorch decal: a dark star PlaneGeometry(.22,.22) under the switch at y+.016.
- Keep the switch's toon material unchanged throughout, so its silhouette stays visible.
findings.verify: Rerun d-drive.mjs crops 70–73. At +0.1 s the switch body (dark block) and the ACROSS SWITCH dashed socket must remain distinguishable (luma contrast ≥40 between the switch and the board). At +0.4 s no area larger than 40×40 px may be above luma 240.
findings.verify_reason: The code is as cited: arcCore hot('#e8f8ff',3), glow size .7 at opacity .8 (re-randomised to .5–1.0 each frame, station.ts:411), arcLight 6–16 intensity (station.ts:407), and arcT .6 s (station.ts:390). I reproduced it: verify-garage-models-08-arc and -09-arc-later (+0.45 s after the switch opens) show the SWITCH body and the ACROSS SWITCH socket bleached into a pale blob, with the left board tinted. That is well past DR-79's 120 ms near a taught part. I keep P1 because it hides the exact part being taught at the moment of failure, and it has been open since research F4.
findings.fix_correction: Also cap the per-frame random opacity at station.ts:411 (currently .5+rand*.5) and the light at station.ts:407 (6+rand*10). Those per-frame lines override the constructor values, so changing only lines 186-189 will not take effect.

findings.title: Pip disappears behind the 2.2 m cabinet columns and the bench scope; none of the garage fixtures are occluders
findings.fix:
1) In game.ts addProp, push every prop mesh taller than 1.2 m (prefab size[1] ≥ 1.2: cabinet, plant, bookshelf, vending, mop, lamp, dolly; plus stacked boxes whose y+h > 1.5) into an occluder list using an alpha-hash fade, so it stays sorted (see DR-78).
2) Register the station's scope body (station.ts:170) and the garage chest and cabinets via a helper `fadeable(mesh)`.
3) Cast three rays (feet .2, chest .9, head 1.6) instead of one at p.y+.4.
4) Add a keep-out lane around the bench and stand back. garage.ts:32-33 add {points:[[-2.6,-4.8],[2.6,-4.8]],r:1.3}, so no clutter column spawns at (-1.6, -4.91).
findings.verify: Rerun b-close.mjs set 2. In garage-models-41 at least 70% of Pip's pixels must remain visible, or the column must be at opacity ≤ .25 within .2 s. After the lane change, g.audit() must no longer list 'cabinet @-1.6,-4.91'.
findings.verify_reason: Occluders are only pillars and interior walls (decor.ts:48,55) plus game.box(fade) (game.ts:113), and the ray is a single one to p.y+.4 (game.ts:387). In garage-models-41 Pip is hidden behind the cabinet column with only the hat crown showing, and no fade happens; there is no silhouette or x-ray pass in src. DR-12 explicitly covers cabinets taller than 1.2 m. Correction: the claim that a column sits 'in the robot's carry path between the pad and the stand' is wrong. The pad is at x 6.4 and the stand at 0.7, while the column is at x -1.6, beyond the stand (my carry in -05/-06 never passes it). In -38 Pip is only partly hidden by the scope.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/verify-garage-models-06-carry-mid.jpg (carry route does not pass the -1.6 column)
findings.fix_correction: Prop meshes use cached, shared toon() materials, so fading one prop would fade every mesh of that colour. Each faded prop needs cloned materials (or a per-instance dither/alpha-hash uniform), as decor.ts:47 does for walls. The bench desk is built on g.decorRoot (station.ts:116), and freeze(decorRoot) (game.ts:105) merges it, so any fixture that must fade has to be built on game.root instead. The lane in item 4 is fine.

findings.title: False affordances: extra cable reels, a splitter and a cable dolly in a room with no cable task
findings.fix:
1) garage.ts:31: replace both 'parts' entries with a garage-specific recipe `spares` in clutter.ts: a crate, a tyre stack (torus as in room.ts:95, kind 'box' physics), a small oil can (bin kind with color '#e5484d'), and a cone.

findings.title: Cardboard boxes in teal, yellow and grey-blue read as plastic tubs; every box is the same size with the same tape and label (copy-paste look)
findings.verify: Retake garage-models-18/-33. No two adjacent boxes share size, label position and colour. No non-kraft box appears. Add a unit test over makeProp('box', c, v) for v in 0..5 that asserts distinct bounding boxes for at least 3 variants.
findings.verify_reason: The box prefab has one size .7×.6×.7 (prefabs.ts:10), and build('box') ignores variant: the tape and label are always in the same place (prefabs.ts:56-61). The palette and the level props put teal, yellow and grey-blue boxes in the room (garage.ts:11,31). The start and dock shots show rows of identical cubes with identical labels, and the grey-blue and teal ones read as plastic tubs.
findings.fix_correction: Size variants change the physics collider, because prefab size drives the cuboid. The boxSizes table must feed collider creation in addProp as well as the mesh, or stacks will float or sink.

findings.title: Floor lamps read as yellow pennant flags: the shade is an open, zero-thickness cone seen from below
findings.verify: Retake garage-models-23 and -40 (zoom 9, orbit 180°). The lamp head must read as a cup-shaped work light from both sides, with an ink rim visible.

findings.title: TEST STAND sign is a single-sided plane: it vanishes from behind, leaving a bare post
findings.problem:
The TEST STAND sign is `new T.PlaneGeometry(1.2,.3)` with flat() (MeshBasic, FrontSide) on game.root at (STAND.x, .9, STAND.z-.9) = (0.7, .9, -5.35), tilted -.2 (room.ts:78). Its post is a separate box(.06,.8,.06) on the stand group at local (0, .4, -.85) (room.ts:79), so it ends at y .8, below the sign's centre, about 2 cm in front of the plane.

The sign has no backing board and no housing. Orbiting 180° shows the post with nothing on it (garage-models-13-test-stand-o180, -39). The front view shows a flat label floating above a thin stick. DR-63 requires signs to have housings, and DR-72 requires them to be mounted.
findings.verify: Retake garage-models-13 (orbit 180°). The sign board must be visible from the back, as a dark board or a second plaque, attached to the post with no gap.
findings.verify_reason: room.ts:78 makes the sign a PlaneGeometry with flat(), a MeshBasicMaterial with default FrontSide (kit.ts:61), on game.root with no backing. In garage-models-13 (orbit 180) only the bare DMETAL post stands behind the stand. The sign is single-sided.

findings.title: Rolling road is four short stubs that read as tombstones; the bench harness ends inside the robot's wheel
findings.problem:
Rollers: room.ts:77 builds four separate cyl(.12,.12,.2,18,'z') pale '#9aa3b2' stubs on dark DMETAL blocks at (±.36, .18, ±.33). Each is only 20 cm long. From the side and behind (garage-models-13, -39, -78) they look like little grey tombstones or mushrooms half sunk into a black slab, not a rolling road. Real dyno stands have two long knurled drums per axle.

Harness: the red TubeGeometry harness (room.ts:81-82) runs from (1.35, .95, -3.05) to (1.05, .3, -4.1).
- Its start is inside the bench top: the desk's back face is at z -3.075 and its top at y 1.035, so it emerges from inside the cabinet under the parts tray, not from the harness board.
- Its end sits at the robot's rear-right wheel contact point. That wheel is at world (1.06, .45, -4.12) with radius .15, spanning y .30–.60, so the harness terminates in the tyre (garage-models-39 shows the red tube ending on a roller; -52 shows it disappearing under the robot).

The teaching claim 'wired to the bench' has no visible connector.
findings.fix:
1) Replace the 4 stubs with 2 drums per axle: cyl(.11,.11,1.0,24,'z') at local (±.36, .17, 0) in DMETAL, with 6 thin INK knurl rings (cyl r .112, h .01) along each. Sink them into a recessed slot: two INK boxes (1.1, .02, .26) at y .141.

findings.title: Garage draw calls ~1156 at start and in survey (target ≤ ~250)
findings.problem: snap().drawCalls returned 1156 at the start view and 1156 in the survey, at 60 fps on the host GPU. The count includes every composer and outline pass. DR-24 sets ≤ about 250 at the game camera; Lunch was brought from 1090 to about 175 by merging. The garage dresses most fixtures as many small parts on decorRoot, but the station root (bench board, traces, sockets, labels: each sign() is its own MeshBasic material via cachedLabel) and the three robotMesh copies (about 40 meshes each, with per-call toon() materials) are not frozen. Performance holds on this GPU, but a weaker GPU or a laptop will not.
findings.fix:
1) Run kit freeze() on the static parts of the bench (desk, board base, traces, socket pads, label posts) by moving them under a static group. Keep clickables, the fuse, lamps, dots and the arc live.
2) Build the two decor robots into decorRoot so the level's freeze merges them, or instance them.
3) Share one MeshBasicMaterial per label texture across signs (the cached texture already exists; cache the material too).
findings.verify: snap().drawCalls ≤ 300 at start and survey. fps unchanged at 60. tests/station-garage.spec.ts still passes.
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced the count: garage snap().drawCalls = 1156 at start and in survey, at fps 60, with both fullfx and lowfx. The comparison in the finding is wrong, though. Lunch measures 1297 (fullfx) and 1341 (lowfx), and meeting 1275, by the same counter (game.ts:450-451 counts every composer and outline pass). Lunch is not at about 175, and the garage is actually below the other rooms. This is a game-wide DR-24 miss, not a garage regression.
findings.fix_correction: Treat this as cross-room. First establish what DR-24's 250 counts: this counter includes outline and shadow passes, so roughly 2–3× the scene meshes. Garage-only merging will not reach ≤300 on this counter. The proposed merges (bench statics, decor robots on decorRoot, shared label materials) are still valid savings.

findings.title: Prompt says 'E Work at the bench' before the robot is on the stand, contradicting the card
findings.problem: Standing at the bench before step 1 is done, the prompt reads 'E Work at the bench' (garage-models-14-bench-front, -15). The card still says 'Carry the delivery robot onto the test stand behind the bench', and the marker is on the robot. GarageBench.prompt returns 'Fetch the robot' when !onStand (station.ts:460), but the game's bench-proximity prompt wins. Sitting then only produces 'Robot not on the stand' on the scope.
findings.fix: In the game's bench-prompt branch, when the station exposes a `ready()` gate (add `ready(){return this.onStand}` to GarageBench), show the station's own prompt ('Fetch the robot') instead of 'Work at the bench'. Alternatively, block sitting until onStand and play the existing 'hm' voice.
findings.verify: Retake garage-models-14. With the robot on its pad, the prompt at the bench must name the robot, not the bench.
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced it. Walking to the bench before carrying the robot gives the prompt 'E Work at the bench' while the card says 'Carry the delivery robot…' (verify-garage-models-03). Pressing E sits Pip down, the prompt becomes 'Fetch the robot', and the scope shows 'Robot not on the stand' (verify-04). The cause is wrong in the finding: no game-level prompt wins. It is GarageBench.prompt itself, whose !atBench branch at station.ts:457 returns 'Work at the bench' regardless of onStand. Sitting early also ticks the 'Sit at the garage bench' step (done: this.active, station.ts:98) before step 1.
extra_evidence: v1.mjs log: 'PROMPT at bench before robot: EWork at the bench', after sitting 'EFetch the robot'
findings.fix_correction: Change station.ts:457 to `if(near)return this.onStand?{key:'E',text:'Work at the bench'}:null;` (or a non-E hint toward the robot), so the bench never offers E before the robot is on the stand. No new ready() gate in game.ts is needed. Optionally make step 2's done() require onStand: `()=>(this.active&&this.onStand)||this.logged.length>0`.

notes.fun:
The physical payoff is the right idea. Carrying the robot onto a rolling road and then watching it drive a painted delivery lane around the room is a real Good Job-style toy moment. At the default zoom the drive reads well: the robot shows its face while driving, the wheels spin and the route loops past the clutter (garage-models-76). But the fun is undercut in three places.
- The win camera frames an empty bench and stand instead of the arriving robot and green dock lamp (garage-models-77/78).
- During the drive, a player at zoom 9 sees almost none of it.
- The robot is one of three identical bots, with no visible fault before you fix it.

The arc and dizzy reboot are good slapstick ideas, but they happen edge-on to the bench camera or bleach into a white blob. Chaos is still limited to knocking crates, cones and bins about. The bins visibly tip over just from Pip walking (garage-models-10, -12), which is nice incidental physics. There is no designed chaos shortcut in this station room.
notes.playability:
The intended route works end to end with the spec's coordinates: pad → (3.4,-4) → (2.5,-4.4) drop, which snaps within 2.6 m; then (2.9,-1.1) → bench E. All 3 jobs pass at tier 3 and the room is won at about 25–29 s game time. There were zero console or page errors in 5 runs.

Friction found:
- Pip vanishes behind 2.2 m cabinet columns and behind the bench scope, because none of them fade (garage-models-38, -41).
- A clutter cabinet column and crates crowd the stand's back.
- One walk stalled against the decor robot's solid at (8.4, -5.2) (b-close log).
- The prompt says 'Work at the bench' before the robot is placed.
- Draw calls are about 1156.

g.audit(.04) is clean. g.audit(.02) reports only the two stacked cabinet+box pairs, at (-1.6,-4.91) and (-8.21,3.21), depth .02.
notes.clarity: Clarity suffers mostly from colour. Job yellow '#ffc629' is in the garage clutter palette, so yellow crates, yellow cabinet columns, yellow mail carts, a yellow chair and a yellow reel surround the yellow job items and the yellow marker (about 2.8% of the play-area pixels at start). The job robot is visually identical to the decor robot next to it. The marker is a pale translucent un-outlined cone that rides on the carried robot instead of pointing at the stand. False-affordance reels, a splitter and a cable dolly invite 'Grab the splitter' in a room with no cable. Bench labels are 7–8 px at 1440×900. On the plus side, the bench view is uncluttered and the scope trace is large and legible.
notes.models:
Strong models:
- The delivery robot (robotMesh) has about 8 cues: spoked wheels, a dark chassis with yellow bumpers, a glossy teal body, a cream cargo bin with a yellow lid and handle slot, a head with a dark face screen and glowing eyes, and an antenna lamp. It reads at the game camera and looks charming when its face is visible.
- The bench board is detailed and honest.
- The roller door and the tyre stacks read correctly.
- The mop bucket, coolbox and chairs are well built.

Weak models:
- The floor lamps read as yellow flags (open zero-thickness cone).
- The rolling road is four stubby tombstone rollers.
- The TEST STAND sign is a one-sided plane that vanishes from behind.
- The wall chargers are blank cream plaques with no cable.
- The parcel shelves have only front posts.
- The bench cabinet front and back, the scope back, the tool-chest back and the side-cabinet backs are large blank faces.
- Cardboard boxes are one size with an identical tape+label layout in five colours, including teal, yellow and grey-blue, which read as plastic tubs.

Outlines are present and dark enough on most props (darkest-2% luma about 20–30 on cabinets and the robot; Pip about 56). Floors remain near-white (median 214–226, both rim and norim), so contact shadows and value separation are weak. The teal lounge rug at (-6.8, 4.4) is an office prop out of place in a service garage; a rubber anti-fatigue mat would fit better. The Pip helmet ridge ('cat-ear' fin, DR-64) is still visible from behind and at the win (garage-models-15, -66); that is a cross-room Pip issue.
